name: Propylene Glycol Esters of Fatty Acids
aliases: E477, INS 477, propylene glycol esters of fatty acids, propane-1,2-diol esters of fatty acids, propylene glycol fatty acid esters
what_is: Emulsifiers made by combining propylene glycol with fatty acids. During digestion they can be hydrolysed into propylene glycol and fatty acids.
why_botia: These emulsifiers break down into fatty acids and propylene glycol — the same compound used in food-system antifreeze and theatrical fog machines. That is why JECFA sets the intake limit in terms of the propylene glycol released, not the whole additive: that is what is being tracked. They are used, among other products, in industrial bakery products and ice cream.
can_1: Detect E477 and the principal propylene-glycol ester names used on labels.
can_2: Explain that JECFA expresses the intake limit as released propylene glycol and show the Texture and E-number layers.
cannot_1: Determine how much E477 or how much propylene glycol a product will release from the ingredient list alone.
cannot_2: Determine the exact fatty-acid composition or manufacturing feedstock from the declared name.

title: Propylene Glycol Esters of Fatty Acids
description: E477 emulsifiers break down into fatty acids and propylene glycol. JECFA sets an ADI of 0–25 mg/kg body weight expressed as propylene glycol.
